question: Explain the core architecture of Angular (Modules, Components, Templates, Metadata, Services, Dependency Injection).
idealAnswer: Angular is an enterprise TypeScript framework built around Components (UI logic & templates), Services (business logic & HTTP), and hierarchical Dependency Injection, traditionally grouped in NgModules or Standalone Components.
ideal_answer: Angular is an enterprise TypeScript framework built around Components (UI logic & templates), Services (business logic & HTTP), and hierarchical Dependency Injection, traditionally grouped in NgModules or Standalone Components.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Architecture and Angular Architecture Overview comprehension.

question: What are Standalone Components in Angular 14+, and how do they eliminate the requirement for NgModules?
idealAnswer: Standalone components set 'standalone: true' and declare their own dependencies in an 'imports' array, simplifying application structure, improving tree-shaking, and removing the boilerplate of creating NgModules.
ideal_answer: Standalone components set 'standalone: true' and declare their own dependencies in an 'imports' array, simplifying application structure, improving tree-shaking, and removing the boilerplate of creating NgModules.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Modern Angular and Standalone Components comprehension.

question: Explain Dependency Injection (DI) in Angular, hierarchical injectors, and service provision scopes (providedIn: 'root' vs component level).
idealAnswer: Angular DI uses a hierarchical injector tree. Services providedIn: 'root' are application-wide singletons. Services provided at component level instantiate a new service instance scoped exclusively to that component and its children.
ideal_answer: Angular DI uses a hierarchical injector tree. Services providedIn: 'root' are application-wide singletons. Services provided at component level instantiate a new service instance scoped exclusively to that component and its children.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Dependency Injection and Hierarchical Dependency Injection comprehension.

question: What is Change Detection in Angular, and how does ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush improve performance over Default?
idealAnswer: Angular's change detection checks if model values changed to update the DOM. Default strategy checks all components on every browser event. OnPush strategy checks a component only when an @Input() reference changes, an event originates within it, or an async pipe emits.
ideal_answer: Angular's change detection checks if model values changed to update the DOM. Default strategy checks all components on every browser event. OnPush strategy checks a component only when an @Input() reference changes, an event originates within it, or an async pipe emits.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Change Detection and Default vs OnPush Change Detection comprehension.

question: Explain Angular Signals (signal, computed, effect) introduced in Angular 16+ and how they enable fine-grained reactivity without Zone.js.
idealAnswer: Signals are reactive value wrappers that track reads and trigger precise updates. Unlike Zone.js which triggers broad dirty-checking passes across component trees, Signals enable fine-grained reactivity and Zoneless Angular.
ideal_answer: Signals are reactive value wrappers that track reads and trigger precise updates. Unlike Zone.js which triggers broad dirty-checking passes across component trees, Signals enable fine-grained reactivity and Zoneless Angular.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Modern Angular and Angular Signals & Zoneless Reactivity comprehension.

question: What is the difference between Reactive Forms (FormGroup, FormControl) and Template-Driven Forms in Angular?
idealAnswer: Reactive Forms manage form state programmatically in TypeScript using FormGroups and FormControls with synchronous, immutable data streams and easy unit testing. Template-Driven Forms rely on two-way binding ([(ngModel)]) in templates.
ideal_answer: Reactive Forms manage form state programmatically in TypeScript using FormGroups and FormControls with synchronous, immutable data streams and easy unit testing. Template-Driven Forms rely on two-way binding ([(ngModel)]) in templates.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Forms and Reactive vs Template-Driven Forms comprehension.

question: Explain RxJS Observables, Observers, and common operators (map, filter, switchMap, mergeMap, debounceTime) in Angular.
idealAnswer: RxJS handles asynchronous event streams. switchMap cancels previous in-flight inner observables on new emission (ideal for search autocomplete); mergeMap processes all inner observables concurrently; debounceTime delays emissions until a quiet interval.
ideal_answer: RxJS handles asynchronous event streams. switchMap cancels previous in-flight inner observables on new emission (ideal for search autocomplete); mergeMap processes all inner observables concurrently; debounceTime delays emissions until a quiet interval.
explanation: Evaluates Angular RxJS and RxJS Operators & Streams comprehension.

question: What is the 'async' pipe in Angular templates, and why is it preferred over manual Observable subscription?
idealAnswer: The async pipe automatically subscribes to Observables or Promises, returns latest emitted values to template, marks OnPush components for check, and automatically unsubscribes on component destruction to prevent memory leaks.
ideal_answer: The async pipe automatically subscribes to Observables or Promises, returns latest emitted values to template, marks OnPush components for check, and automatically unsubscribes on component destruction to prevent memory leaks.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Templates & RxJS and Async Pipe Benefits comprehension.

question: Explain Component Lifecycle Hooks in Angular (ngOnInit, ngOnChanges, ngAfterViewInit, ngOnDestroy) and their execution order.
idealAnswer: ngOnChanges runs on input changes; ngOnInit runs after initial input binding; ngAfterViewInit runs after component view and child views initialize (safe for DOM queries); ngOnDestroy runs before destruction for cleanup.
ideal_answer: ngOnChanges runs on input changes; ngOnInit runs after initial input binding; ngAfterViewInit runs after component view and child views initialize (safe for DOM queries); ngOnDestroy runs before destruction for cleanup.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Lifecycle and Component Lifecycle Hooks comprehension.

question: What are Directives in Angular: Structural Directives (*ngIf, *ngFor, or new @if/@for control flow) vs Attribute Directives (ngClass, ngStyle)?
idealAnswer: Structural directives alter DOM layout by adding or removing elements (*ngIf, *ngFor, or Angular 17+ built-in control flow @if/@for). Attribute directives alter the appearance or behavior of existing DOM elements (ngClass, custom directives).
ideal_answer: Structural directives alter DOM layout by adding or removing elements (*ngIf, *ngFor, or Angular 17+ built-in control flow @if/@for). Attribute directives alter the appearance or behavior of existing DOM elements (ngClass, custom directives).
explanation: Evaluates Angular Directives and Structural vs Attribute Directives comprehension.

question: What are Pipes in Angular, and what is the difference between Pure and Impure Pipes?
idealAnswer: Pipes transform template values (e.g. {{ date | date:'short' }}). Pure pipes execute only when primitive input values or object references change (cached and fast). Impure pipes execute on every single change detection cycle (expensive).
ideal_answer: Pipes transform template values (e.g. {{ date | date:'short' }}). Pure pipes execute only when primitive input values or object references change (cached and fast). Impure pipes execute on every single change detection cycle (expensive).
explanation: Evaluates Angular Pipes and Pure vs Impure Pipes comprehension.

question: Explain Angular Routing: Route Guards (CanActivate, CanDeactivate, Resolve) and Lazy Loading with loadChildren.
idealAnswer: Angular Router configures URL navigation. Route Guards protect routes based on auth (CanActivate) or warn unsaved changes (CanDeactivate). Lazy loading (loadChildren: () => import(...)) splits feature bundles so modules/components load only on navigation.
ideal_answer: Angular Router configures URL navigation. Route Guards protect routes based on auth (CanActivate) or warn unsaved changes (CanDeactivate). Lazy loading (loadChildren: () => import(...)) splits feature bundles so modules/components load only on navigation.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Routing and Route Guards & Lazy Loading comprehension.

question: What is ViewEncapsulation in Angular (Emulated, ShadowDom, None), and how does Emulated scoping work?
idealAnswer: ViewEncapsulation controls CSS scoping. Emulated (default) simulates Shadow DOM by appending unique host attributes (_ngcontent-xxx) to elements and selectors. ShadowDom uses real browser Shadow DOM. None leaves CSS global.
ideal_answer: ViewEncapsulation controls CSS scoping. Emulated (default) simulates Shadow DOM by appending unique host attributes (_ngcontent-xxx) to elements and selectors. ShadowDom uses real browser Shadow DOM. None leaves CSS global.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Styling & DOM and ViewEncapsulation Modes comprehension.

question: Explain HTTP Interceptors (HttpInterceptorFn) in Angular and common use cases like attaching JWT tokens or logging.
idealAnswer: HTTP Interceptors intercept outgoing HttpRequest and incoming HttpResponse globally, allowing automatic attachment of Authorization Bearer JWT headers, centralized error handling, and request retry logic.
ideal_answer: HTTP Interceptors intercept outgoing HttpRequest and incoming HttpResponse globally, allowing automatic attachment of Authorization Bearer JWT headers, centralized error handling, and request retry logic.

question: What are Content Projection (<ng-content>) and ViewChild/ContentChild queries in Angular?
idealAnswer: <ng-content> projects external HTML content into component template slots (transclusion). @ViewChild queries elements/components in the component's own template; @ContentChild queries elements projected into the component via <ng-content>.
ideal_answer: <ng-content> projects external HTML content into component template slots (transclusion). @ViewChild queries elements/components in the component's own template; @ContentChild queries elements projected into the component via <ng-content>.
explanation: Evaluates Angular Component Design and Content Projection & ViewChild comprehension.
